# llms.txt — Aerial onboarding for AI agents

This file tells an AI agent how to install, configure, and verify Aerial
(the control tower for autonomous agent fleets) on the machine it is
running on. Follow the steps in order. Every command is safe to re-run.

## What Aerial is

An operations layer over your existing agent harness: a ticket hub (the
system of record), an ops agent that detects failures and applies
governed fixes, an operator console, built-in reporting, and fleet
management for local model seats. MIT licensed, fully local, no telemetry.

## Repo layout

- `hub/` — the ticket hub (FastAPI service, SQLite storage, port 8020)
- `dashboard/` — operator console (:8777), daily board, ops agent loop
- `integration/` — scheduler, shadow-hierarchy runner
- `bin/aerial_verify.py` — end-to-end chain check
- `config/deployment.yaml.example` — configuration template

## Install steps

### 1. Requirements

Python 3.10+ and curl. No third-party runtime dependencies for the core
services. Docker optional (the hub can run bare).

### 2. Configuration

```bash
cp config/deployment.yaml.example config/deployment.yaml
mkdir -p ~/.aerial/secrets ~/.aerial/logs ~/.aerial/data
head -c 32 /dev/urandom | xxd -p -c 64 > ~/.aerial/secrets/hub-token
chmod 600 ~/.aerial/secrets/hub-token
```

The only values worth changing on first boot: `cluster.node_name`
(prefix for job ids) and — later — `email.recipient_email` (empty =
delivery disabled).

### 3. Start the ticket hub

```bash
TICKET_HUB_HOME=$HOME/.aerial/hub-home python3 hub/api.py
```

Health check: `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8020/health` → `{"ok": true, ...}`.
Hub auth tokens live at `cluster.hub_token_file` (default
`~/.aerial/secrets/hub-token`).

### 4. Start the operator console

```bash
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$PWD/dashboard"
python3 dashboard/serve_console.py
```

Console: `http://127.0.0.1:8777/dashboard` — bearer-authed with the same
hub token. Health: `/dashboard/health`.

### 5. Verify the chain

```bash
python3 bin/aerial_verify.py
```

All rows ✓ = the chain is live. The ops agent and scheduler are started
the same way (`dashboard/followup/runner.py --interval 300`,
`integration/scheduler.py --interval 30`); systemd unit examples are in
docs/GETTING-STARTED.md.

## Adding a model seat (BYOM)

Edit `dashboard/vram_registry.json`: add a seat entry with `name`,
`port`, `service_unit`, and `load_cmd`. The ops agent probes every seat
each cycle; a seat that does not answer is a finding, not a crash.

## Common failure modes

- `ModuleNotFoundError: dashboard` → export
  `PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$PWD/dashboard"` from the repo root
- `FileNotFoundError` under `~/.aerial/...` → create the parent
  directories (see step 2)
- Console returns 401 → every request needs
  `Authorization: Bearer <hub-token>`
- Board shows degraded sections → they fill as the ops agent accumulates
  data; the first daily render is `dashboard/render_daily.py`
